## Problem

## Requirements

- Input: an integer array `priorities`; entry `priorities[i]` gives the priority assigned to process `i`.
- The CPU runs processes from the highest index down to the lowest: `n-1, n-2, ..., 0`.
- Every process consumes one time unit to run.
- Process `i` is starved when there exists a later-indexed process `j` with a smaller priority value, meaning `j > i` and `priorities[j] < priorities[i]`.
- Its starvation interval starts when the first such lower-priority process begins running and finishes when process `i` starts running, at the beginning of its one-unit execution.
- Return the starvation duration for each process.

## Hints

<details>
<summary>Hint 1</summary>

Starvation occurs when a process with lower priority is scheduled after a process with higher priority but later index, think of it as a condition on the suffix of the array.

</details>

<details>
<summary>Hint 2</summary>

For each process i, check if there exists any j > i with priorities[j] < priorities[i], if so, the starvation time is the earliest such j's index minus i.

</details>

<details>
<summary>Hint 3</summary>

The complexity target is O(n) using a monotonic stack or scanning from right to left to track the minimum priority seen so far.

</details>
